name: DynamoDBService
title: DynamoDB Service
description: Give an agent the full DynamoDB operation set on a table
whenToUse: Reach for this when an agent needs to look things up and record them as it goes, forming its own reads and writes rather than following one fixed lookup: fetch a record by key, read a range, store or amend one. A single known read or write in a fixed place is cheaper done inline. Attach it to the agent by a service edge.

defaultTable.title: Default Table
defaultTable.description: The table every method uses unless the caller names another. Required, so an agent that omits a table still acts somewhere deliberate rather than failing.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: aws-dynamodb
package.packageFile:
# THE FIRST AWS PACKAGE AS MANIFESTS, and what proves `awsSigV4`.
#
# DynamoDB's HTTP API is one endpoint per region, an `X-Amz-Target` header naming the
# operation, and a JSON body. There is nothing else to it: take the signer and the
# translator out of @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb and that is what remains. The client, its
# cache and its four Command classes collapse into one call per node.
#
# TWO EXECUTOR CAPABILITIES CARRY IT, both using AWS's own libraries rather than anything
# written here:
#   awsSigV4              signs the request (@smithy/signature-v4)
#   encoding: dynamodbJson  translates values to and from DynamoDB's type tags
#                         (@aws-sdk/util-dynamodb, the same translator the DocumentClient
#                         uses). It cannot be an expression: the walk is recursive.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/aws-dynamodb/`.

name: aws-dynamodb
displayName: AWS DynamoDB
description: Read and write records in AWS DynamoDB
version: 2.0.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751473913/gravity/icons/DynamoDB.png

features:
  - Put a record, read one by key
  - Query and scan on demand over a service edge
  - Signed with AWS Signature Version 4, no SDK in the node

# Regional endpoints, one subdomain level: dynamodb.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com.
allowedHosts:
  - "**.amazonaws.com"

requires:
  credential: [awsSigV4]
  transport: [json]
  executorVersion: ">=1.2.0"

credentials.awsCredential.yaml:
# Transcribed from plugin-base's shared AWSCredential, NAME AND FIELDS UNCHANGED so
# credentials already stored against `awsCredential` keep resolving. Every AWS package
# shares this one, exactly as they shared the TypeScript definition.
#
# sessionToken is NEW, and additive. The retired definition had no such field, so anyone on
# temporary credentials (an assumed role, anything via STS) could not use these nodes at
# all. The signer sends and signs it only when it is filled in.

name: awsCredential
displayName: AWS Credentials
description: AWS credentials for AWS services (DynamoDB, S3, Bedrock, and the rest)
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html

properties:
  - name: accessKeyId
    displayName: Access Key ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Access Key ID
    placeholder: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
  - name: secretAccessKey
    displayName: Secret Access Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Secret Access Key
    placeholder: ""
  - name: region
    displayName: AWS Region
    type: string
    secret: false # Public: it appears in every AWS endpoint hostname.
    required: false
    default: us-east-1
    description: The region your tables live in
    placeholder: us-east-1
  - name: sessionToken
    displayName: Session Token
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: true
    description: Only for temporary credentials from STS or an assumed role. Leave empty for a long-lived key.
    placeholder: ""

shared.dynamodb.yaml:
# The one call shape every DynamoDB operation shares.
#
# There is no per-operation URL: everything goes to the regional endpoint and the
# `X-Amz-Target` header picks the operation. A node $refs this and adds that header plus a
# body, which is why these manifests read like RPC rather than REST.

call: &call
  method: POST
  url: "return 'https://dynamodb.' + credentials.awsCredential.region + '.amazonaws.com/'"

  credential:
    scheme: awsSigV4
    service: dynamodb

  headers:
    # AWS's own JSON dialect, NOT application/json. The wrong one is a 400 that complains
    # about the body rather than the header, which sends you looking in the wrong place.
    Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0

  transport: json
  # Plain JSON in the manifest; type tags on the wire. See api.schema.json#encoding.
  encoding: dynamodbJson

  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    # DynamoDB reports throttling as a 400 with a specific error type, not a 429. A blanket
    # 400 retry would resend genuinely malformed requests forever, so only the server-side
    # statuses are retried and a throughput problem surfaces instead of being hidden.
    on: [500, 502, 503, 504]

files.api/service.yaml:
# The six methods an agent can call.
#
# FIRST IMPLEMENTATIONS, not transcriptions: the retired node advertised all six and had no
# handlers at all. The descriptions matter as much as the calls, because they are what a
# model reads when deciding which to reach for.
#
# Every method takes an optional `table` and falls back to the configured default, so an
# agent can stay on one table without repeating it and still reach another deliberately.
#
# Values are written PLAIN throughout. `encoding: dynamodbJson` on the shared call adds the
# type tags going out and strips them coming back, so neither an agent nor this file ever
# writes {"S": ...}.

put:
  description: >-
    Write one item. Overwrites any existing item with the same key unless a condition says
    otherwise. Returns the key that was written.
  calls:
    - $ref: dynamodb#call
      name: written
      headers:
        X-Amz-Target: DynamoDB_20120810.PutItem
        Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0
      body:
        TableName: "return params.table || config.defaultTable"
        Item: "return params.item || {}"
        ConditionExpression: "return params.condition || undefined"
  returns: "return { ok: true, table: params.table || config.defaultTable, item: params.item }"

get:
  description: >-
    Read one item by its full key. Pass every key attribute the table has (partition, and
    sort if there is one). Returns found: false when nothing is stored there, which is an
    answer rather than an error.
  calls:
    - $ref: dynamodb#call
      name: item
      headers:
        X-Amz-Target: DynamoDB_20120810.GetItem
        Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0
      body:
        TableName: "return params.table || config.defaultTable"
        Key: "return params.key || {}"
  returns: "return { ok: true, found: !!response.Item, item: response.Item || null }"

query:
  description: >-
    Read items from ONE partition, which is the efficient way to read a range. `keyCondition`
    is a DynamoDB expression over the key, e.g. "userId = :u AND createdAt > :since", with
    the values supplied in `values` as { ":u": "user-1", ":since": "2026-01-01" }. To read a
    secondary index, name it in `index`. Use scan only when you cannot express a partition.
  calls:
    - $ref: dynamodb#call
      name: rows
      headers:
        X-Amz-Target: DynamoDB_20120810.Query
        Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0
      body:
        TableName: "return params.table || config.defaultTable"
        IndexName: "return params.index || undefined"
        KeyConditionExpression: "return params.keyCondition"
        FilterExpression: "return params.filter || undefined"
        ExpressionAttributeValues: "return params.values || undefined"
        # Only for names that collide with DynamoDB's reserved words, which is what the
        # #placeholder syntax in an expression refers to.
        ExpressionAttributeNames: "return params.names || undefined"
        # BOUNDED BY DEFAULT. An agent asking a broad question should not pull a whole
        # partition into a model's context, and 25 is a page a person would read.
        Limit: "return params.limit || 25"
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      items: response.Items || [],
      count: (response.Items || []).length,
      more: !!response.LastEvaluatedKey
    }

scan:
  description: >-
    Read across the WHOLE table, optionally filtered. Slow and expensive on anything large,
    because it reads every item before filtering. Prefer query whenever the partition is
    known. Returns at most `limit` items, 25 by default.
  calls:
    - $ref: dynamodb#call
      name: rows
      headers:
        X-Amz-Target: DynamoDB_20120810.Scan
        Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0
      body:
        TableName: "return params.table || config.defaultTable"
        FilterExpression: "return params.filter || undefined"
        ExpressionAttributeValues: "return params.values || undefined"
        ExpressionAttributeNames: "return params.names || undefined"
        Limit: "return params.limit || 25"
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      items: response.Items || [],
      count: (response.Items || []).length,
      more: !!response.LastEvaluatedKey
    }

delete:
  description: >-
    Delete one item by its full key. Succeeds whether or not anything was there, which is
    DynamoDB's behaviour, so a true result does not prove something existed.
  calls:
    - $ref: dynamodb#call
      name: removed
      headers:
        X-Amz-Target: DynamoDB_20120810.DeleteItem
        Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0
      body:
        TableName: "return params.table || config.defaultTable"
        Key: "return params.key || {}"
        ConditionExpression: "return params.condition || undefined"
        # Ask for what was removed, so the caller can tell a real deletion from a no-op.
        ReturnValues: ALL_OLD
  returns: >-
    return {
      ok: true,
      existed: !!response.Attributes,
      deleted: response.Attributes || null
    }

update:
  description: >-
    Change PART of an item without rewriting it. `updateExpression` is a DynamoDB update
    expression, e.g. "SET #n = :name, visits = visits + :one", with values in `values` and
    any reserved-word attribute names in `names` as { "#n": "name" }. Returns the item as it
    stands after the change.
  calls:
    - $ref: dynamodb#call
      name: updated
      headers:
        X-Amz-Target: DynamoDB_20120810.UpdateItem
        Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0
      body:
        TableName: "return params.table || config.defaultTable"
        Key: "return params.key || {}"
        UpdateExpression: "return params.updateExpression"
        ExpressionAttributeValues: "return params.values || undefined"
        ExpressionAttributeNames: "return params.names || undefined"
        ConditionExpression: "return params.condition || undefined"
        ReturnValues: ALL_NEW
  returns: "return { ok: true, item: response.Attributes || null }"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [defaultTable]
  properties:
    defaultTable:
      type: string
      title: Default Table
      description: >-
        The table every method uses unless the caller names another. Required, so an agent
        that omits a table still acts somewhere deliberate rather than failing.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order": [defaultTable]
files.interface.yaml:
# A PURE SERVICE NODE: no inputs, no outputs, only methods. Both keys are OMITTED rather
# than written as empty lists, because an empty `outputs` claims a node emits nothing on a
# port it declared, which is not the same thing as having no ports at all.

credentials:
  - name: awsCredential
    required: true
    displayName: AWS

# `mcp`, where the retired node said `nosql`. The schema's serviceType list is the
# platform's capability list and it holds mcp and embedding, so `nosql` was a value nothing
# implemented — consistent with that node having had no working methods either. These ARE
# MCP tools: an agent discovers them and calls them by name.
serviceConnectors:
  - name: nosqlService
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: true
    methods: [put, get, query, scan, delete, update]
    description: >-
      DynamoDB operations for an agent: write and read items by key, query a partition,
      scan a table, and delete or update a single item.
files.node.yaml:
type: DynamoDBService
kind: PromiseNode
# Drawn as a service card: it is ATTACHED to an agent over a service edge rather than
# wired in sequence, so it has no inputs or outputs of its own.
template: service

name: DynamoDB Service
category: Storage & Data
color: "#FF9900"

description: Give an agent the full DynamoDB operation set on a table

whenToUse: >-
  Reach for this when an agent needs to look things up and record them as it goes, forming
  its own reads and writes rather than following one fixed lookup: fetch a record by key,
  read a range, store or amend one. A single known read or write in a fixed place is
  cheaper done inline. Attach it to the agent by a service edge.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

# NOT AT PARITY WITH WHAT IT REPLACED — IT DOES MORE. The retired TypeScript advertised
# these six methods on its service connector and implemented NONE of them: the executor
# initialised a client, returned {}, and there were no handlers anywhere in the package. An
# agent that called `query` got nothing back, with nothing reporting a problem. These are
# the first working implementations.

capabilities:
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# A service node is exercised by CALLING a method, not by running the graph.
# Reads back what the DynamoDB (put) fixture writes, so run that one first.

testData:
  config:
    defaultTable: Users
  call:
    method: get
    params:
      key:
        universalId: user-1001
  expect:
    # Plain values, not type tags: this is what proves the decode ran.
    result: "return result.ok && result.found && result.item.name === 'Ada Lovelace'"
